utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Gotovina et al. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I'd like to put briefly a few matters on the record, and Madam Usher could already seek to find the witness to be escorted into the courtroom. I would like to put the following things on the record as regards to the Chamber witnesses 4 through 7. On the 26th of February of this year, the Chamber contacted Chamber Witness 7 and Chamber Witness 6 about their appearing as witnesses in these proceedings. On the 3rd of March, 2010, the Chamber granted the Prosecution's request to send requests for assistance to Croatia in respect of Chamber Witness 7 and Chamber Witness 6. On the 1st of April, 2010, the Chamber informed the parties that Chamber Witness 4 and Chamber Witness 5 have been contacted. The Chamber further informed the parties that the Prosecution may, should it so choose, send requests for assistance with regard to Chamber Witness 4 and Chamber Witness 5. On the 29th of March, 2010 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I apologise for a second. I will -- I apologise for a second. I have to finish just a few lines, Witness, and then I'll be with you. You can remain seated for a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, thank you for your patience. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration, of which the text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. And I inform the parties that LiveNote had to be rebooted two times already today, and most likely it will be fixed in approximately 10 minutes from now. If it causes you any insurmountable problems not to be able to scroll up and down, then please inform the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It is fixed on our screens, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is fixed on your screens, yes. The Prosecution has an advantageous position. Witness, I again apologise for dealing with other matters rather than with your testimony, but we had some technical problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber was informed that you do not seek any protective measures. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means that you'll testify publicly and that we'll call you by your own name. Perhaps I first ask you to state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: My name is Stjepan Zinic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zinic, before we continue, I'd like to inform you about the following. This Chamber is aware that there's an ongoing investigation in Croatia about the events in Grubori. The Chamber is also aware that you have given statements, but apparently the statements were taken from you as a witness. The Chamber is not aware of you being a suspect. Is that a correct understanding of your position in the Croatian proceedings?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I appear as a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, Mr. Zinic, it appears to the Chamber, on the basis of evidence we have received until now, that you most likely have been involved in at least the operation on the 25th of August near to the village of Grubori. That is the reason why I would like to inform you that if any of the questions that will be asked would -- where you would expect that answering the question in accordance with the truth might incriminate yourself, then you may object to answering such a question. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you sought any legal advice on this matter?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I have not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you like to seek advice on what that means, your right not to incriminate yourself, or is it perfectly clear to you?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: There is no need. I believe it is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If at any moment you think that you should not answer a question because of your right not to incriminate yourself, you may address me before you answer the question, and then we'll further deal with that matter. In view of the fact that you are not seeking any further legal advice on the matter and that matters apparently are clear to you, I'd like to continue with the examination. Mr. Zinic, could you please state your rank, and could you tell us to what unit you belonged in August 1995?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: At the time, I was a special training instructor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And your unit was?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: The Anti-Terrorist Unit of Lucko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that unit was part of?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Do you mean generally speaking or as part of the operation which took place at the time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In general terms. Would that be a unit of the special police?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was a special police unit of the Croatian Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell us in which operations your unit was involved in late August 1995?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: It took part in Operation Storm and the mopping-up operations during the Obruc-Oluja operation in the area of Knin and Petrova Gora.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I take you to the 25th of August. Do you remember what operation was conducted at that date?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: On that date, the unit was tasked with providing security in the general area of Knin so that the Freedom Train could pass through. During the period of two days, we were also carrying out mopping-up actions and providing security in the area of Knin as well as Plavno and in the area of Ramljani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Plavno operation, was that on the 25th?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the 25th. That was the first day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us what your role was in that operation? What function did you perform?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I took part in that operation, and I was in charge of a group which was assigned a certain axis, although I do not recall the exact locations anymore. In any case, it was in the area of Plavno. We were supposed to mop up terrain and provide security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zinic, how many groups participated in this operation?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think there were four groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us, when you performed this operation, what did your group encounter, what did your group experience?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Specifically, my group found nothing. Nothing happened outside the regular tasks when we went through the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you aware of any incidents which -- not involving your group, any of the other groups?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I heard of certain events which stood out as something that would not have otherwise taken place during such regular operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said you heard of certain events. Could you tell us, did you hear that on the 25th of August or did you hear that at any later stage?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I heard it at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When the operation took place, did you hear any gun-fire?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: It is difficult to recall that period, since it's been a while and I took part in many actions. However, I seem to recall some shooting. Such shootings do take place in the course of such tasks being executed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And as far as your recollection goes, do you have any recollection of what kind of shooting you may have heard? I'm specifically interested in whether you could identify any type of weaponry in this context.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: It is difficult to say precisely, in terms of what types of weapons. In any case, there was shooting from infantry weapons, automatic weapons. There may have been some explosions, too, but I am not certain of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, as far as this shooting is concerned, was that sporadic or was that constant or ...?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: It is difficult for me to say what the intensity of it was. However, since it seems to have occurred on a number of occasions and from different directions, I would say that it was of that nature. Anything more than that is very difficult for me to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please tell me if you don't remember, but any recollection of any Zoljas, for example, which make quite a different sound, or is that not the type of weapons you remember to have heard?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Believe me when I say that it is very difficult for me to tell you if I did hear such a thing or not at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I already invited you to tell me if you don't remember. That's fair. Now, you've heard some shooting. You did not encounter any specific incident. You heard, at a later stage, about incidents encountered or in which other groups may have been engaged. Could you tell us, at the end of the operation, did your group meet at any point with the other groups?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. When the task was completed, in my opinion, all the groups assembled near the final target or the final line we were supposed to reach because we were all supposed to go on leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you supposed to go on leave that day, after the operation would have been concluded?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, not necessarily on leave, as such, but more to rest. We were supposed to go to a location to rest and await new tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, do you remember the place? As you said, final target, I think you mentioned it, the final target or the final line you were supposed to reach, would you meet in a village, would you meet in the fields? Where was that?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think -- well, I can't recall the name of the location, but there seemed to be a number of houses there. It was already dusk by the time we arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember what time it was?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: It's difficult to say. It was before nightfall, perhaps after 8.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you don't remember the name of the location, but you said there seemed to be a number of houses. Was it in such -- could I call it the hamlet? Is that where you met with the other groups?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, more or less a hamlet of sorts. I do recall that we crossed railroad tracks, and having reached a hamlet, we came upon an asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's where you met with the other groups?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, all of the groups assembled there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that in that hamlet or near to that hamlet?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where you met, was that in that hamlet, that group of houses, or was it nearby or at the edge of it? Could you ...

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I seem to recall that we met up on the top of a hill. That's where the groups met and then went down towards the settlement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that the first settlement or hamlet or small village that you entered that day or had there been others?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: On that day, it was the first settlement I entered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, during this operation, were any prisoners taken?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, there weren't any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you talked about the hamlet. Did you see any houses on fire at any time, whether in that hamlet or at any other time during the operation?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I didn't see any. But to the right of where I was, I saw a drill or a stack of smoke which may have come from a building that was on fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you didn't see what was burning, could it have been more houses on fire, or more buildings on fire, I should say?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but you say you saw a drill or a stack of smoke which may have come from a building, you said. Could it have been from more than one building?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, the visibility was rather poor. I cannot determine what the distance was between me and the smoke. I couldn't see a house or houses burning, but it was my assessment that it may have been the result of something being set on fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, did you see that stack of smoke close to the settlement, to the hamlet, the groups of houses you earlier described?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No, no. That was much earlier, much before we went down to the settlement when we met up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you saw this smoke. At a later stage, you met with the others at the top of a hill. And then after you had met with them, you saw then this hamlet or village, group of houses you described?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, no. It was, let's say, at the very beginning of that operation or task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was at the very beginning; the smoke you saw?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, one could hear shooting, after which one could see smoke. There wasn't a lot of smoke. There was some smoke, as it seemed to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that was, you said, rather at the beginning of the operation; is that how I have to understand it?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: In my view, it happened during the first hour, let's say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the operation started at what time?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think sometime in the morning. I think between 9.00 and 10.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: During the operation, did you have any radio contact with the other groups or with the leader of the operation?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I had a Motorola. On a number of occasions, I attempted to contact the others. However, at certain points in time it was impossible to establish radio communication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And at other moments, you were able to establish radio communication?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: It all depended on the lie of the land. Sometimes one could talk to another, but it all depended, let's say, on whether I and my collocutor were closer at that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But on that day, therefore, I understand you had some radio communication, although at some times it was impossible. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us about the content of that radio communication? Was it with other group leaders, was it with the leader of the operation?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, for the most part with other groups. I mean, during the action, I could not establish contact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You could not establish contact with whom; with the operation leader or --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: That's right, the operation leader.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, as far as the content of your communication with the other group leaders is concerned, did you ever discuss the incidents or about the shooting you had heard?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, at one point in time I tried to establish contact and to check what was going on, but I didn't manage at that moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, this Chamber has seen or has access to statements in which other group leaders state that they have heard you, in communication with another group leader, asking what had happened, and they also stated what the answer was, which suggests that there was communication.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I've already said that at some moments, one could talk, and at others, one could not talk. So perhaps I did talk to someone at some point in time, but I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, your earlier answer was that you tried to get in touch -- that you tried to establish contact and to check what was going on, but you did not manage; whereas the statement I just put to you is saying that you asked what happened and that you got an answer, the answer being that the person you were in communication with had encountered Chetniks. Does this refresh your memory in any way?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Believe me, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you exclude for the possibility that you had contact and that you were informed about what had happened or what was happening?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I mean, at that moment, well, believe me, I don't remember. When such tasks were being carried out, even if there were some minor incidents, we didn't really attach much importance to that. We stuck to our own tasks unless some intervention was called for. Believe me, I didn't really think it mattered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zinic, the Chamber had access to a statement which said that at a certain moment all the group leaders were in a village, and that you stood on a plateau in the middle of the village, and that soldiers searched the houses. Is that something you recollect?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I do not really agree to that. At one point, I did state that I came to the edge of something and I saw a house or two. Now, were they houses or whatever, but I thought that it was on the outskirts of the village. Now, whether that village is where that happened, I really cannot say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that was during the operation and before you joined with the other groups, as you said, on the top of a hill? Is that --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to move on. Could you tell us how you were briefed before the operation started? Who briefed you, who gave the tasks; what was said?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, we came to our point of departure, or whatever we're going to call it, and from there we were supposed to set out. The commander -- or, rather, the acting commander, Mr. Josip Celic, told us what our task would be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you get maps?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we did get maps, and we were given the directions in which we were supposed to move.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, there were four groups. May I take it that they moved on parallel in the same direction?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, it's hard to say now. Because of the configuration of the terrain, it was hard to move around and hard to move along parallel lines even within a single group, let alone with other groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the starting point, do you remember where you were; to the left, to the right of -- or in the middle, your group?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I tried to be in the middle as much as possible, but I communicated with all the people there because it was my duty to see whether everything was in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you have responsibility for other groups then as well?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say you tried to be in the middle, and I specifically asked about your group, now, if you have four groups, there are two middle groups, were you to the left -- were you on the left side or on the right side of the middle?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I was to the left of the middle, as it were. My group, well, in relation to my unit, was to the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did not fully understand your answer. You said: "My group, well, in relation to my unit, was to the left." Your group was --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: That's right. I mean, in relation to the unit, my group was to the left. I mean, in relation to the other three groups, I was to the left, in relation to the direction of movement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Most to the left, that means three groups to your right; is that --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you were briefed in the morning. You received your tasks. Did you report to anyone after the operation was concluded?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I think that Mr. Celic asked and that I told him that nothing had happened in relation to my group and the direction that we were to move in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you present when other group leaders reported to Mr. Celic?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you got together on the top of the hill, and then you moved on. At what point in time, then, did you talk to Mr. Celic?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I think it was when we went down, I mean, when we got into this hamlet at the very end of this task, at that moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And where were the other group leaders at that very moment?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, somewhere within that circle, because we were getting close to our vehicles, we were tired, it was raining, so we weren't really paying attention as to who was where.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was Mr. Celic waiting for you at that point in that hamlet or village?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure, but I think that he was there and that he was waiting there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You just told us that you briefly spoke with Mr. Celic and that you reported to him that nothing special had happened. Now, did you discuss this operation with Mr. Celic, or any of the other group leaders, later on on that day or on the next day?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I did not discuss it. It is not customary to discuss tasks. It was stated that nothing had happened, nothing important, so we didn't discuss anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When, for the first time, did you learn that there may have been incidents or problems during this operation on the 25th?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I think it was when we were supposed to write our reports. But that was when we had returned to the headquarters of the unit, but I don't know what date that was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Headquarters of the unit. You're referring to what location?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you said that you were supposed to write your reports. Wasn't it usually done, writing reports, at the end of the operation, such a search operation.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, while such tasks are being carried out, if I, as group leader, assess that there was nothing of interest that was supposed to be written, then I would just report to the commander orally to the effect that nothing had happened, and that would be it. In the field, we did not write up reports straight away. It wasn't really possible, either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to take you to the next day, the 26th of August. I think you earlier said that you conducted an operation in the Ramljani area. Were you involved personally in that operation?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did take part in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you a group leader again or what was your role?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, I was group leader.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you describe what you experienced, what happened during that operation on the 26th?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, we were given the following task: to check the terrain in the area of Ramljani to check whether there were any enemy groups that were still left over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was your task, and what did you experience, what did you encounter that day?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember the details. I know that when we came to some initial position - again I cannot say exactly where that was - we were given maps, and we were supposed to check a particular area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What did you encounter then? I mean, what happened during that day?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: In my group, nothing special happened. We were talking in an area that was inhabited, I mean inhabited -- there would be hamlets consisting of two houses, and three houses, or five houses. I did not really pay any special attention to this if nothing particular happened. We were just walking around, looking. And as we arrived in a hamlet, I noticed that a few houses had been burned. It seems to me that there was still smoke coming out of them, so it seemed that they had burned only recently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any other events worth describing?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any exchange of fire?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: In my group, no. I mean, I can just say that perhaps twice we opened fire at buildings that seemed suspicious to us, that there may have been an enemy there threatening our safety and security. We called that checks for our own security and safety. I mean, you have the feeling that someone may be there, and then fire would be opened from side-arms to check whether there was anyone inside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So on the basis of the mere suspicion that there might be someone in a house or a building, you would open fire?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, no. You see, when you have this suspicion, it has to do with the safety of people. We'd rather open fire than have some of our members shot at from a house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was there no firing at you?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, if there would be no fire, then we wouldn't fire anymore either. We'd move on, continue with the checks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was whether there was any fire in your direction.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No, no, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, what weapons did you have?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, we had our personal side-arms, infantry weapons, and RPG 7 anti-armour rockets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you use those rockets?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, not in that action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you notice any enemies or the presence of any enemies? Did you see any or were you able to observe any enemy movement?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I personally did not, and I believe that no one from my group did either, because had that been the case, I would have known.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you search any houses?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think I entered a few houses, but nothing special.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you find anything in those houses worth mentioning?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I personally did not, but I know that some individuals found some weapons like Zoljas, infantry weapons, boxes with mines, land-mines. I did not really pay much attention to that because that is what could be found in practically every house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The events on that day, were they of a kind that you would give a written report?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember that I wrote a report, but when I last received summons from the state prosecutor in Croatia, I was shown a report that I had written.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we please have P769 on the screen. Could you please have a look at your screen. Is that the report you said that was shown to you?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not quite sure now. I think that in the report that I was shown, there were some words or sentences that had been crossed out. I don't see anything crossed out over here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I see two -- a few words, approximately in the middle, one word in the original, the last line, and four lines from the bottom. Small words are stricken out.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I think that there was more over there, I mean, that there were more things crossed out, but I'm not sure. Judging by the handwriting, it should be mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you recognise your signature at the bottom, or at least your name as written by yourself?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: It is my name, but it's not my signature. However, I cannot say anything for sure now, because the report I saw in Zagreb, I saw very briefly, and I didn't hold it in my own hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The handwriting, is that similar to what you know to be your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I could say that this is my handwriting. I could confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In this report, it is written that when you arrived in the hamlet of Vucenovici, that you came under fire from some houses and that you returned fire, which is in contradiction to the testimony you gave during the last 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I stated that we did fire as we were passing through that settlement, but I cannot recall any details now. I know that in two places, we opened fire. For me, that had to do with safety. Well, we did some things for the sake of our personal safety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I specifically asked you whether you were fired at, and then your answer was that you were not. Here, however, the story is different.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I have to say that it's been a long time since then. Memory fades. But if that is what is written here, it's possible that that may have been the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The report also states that the Chetniks probably fled into the forest, whereas your testimony was that you were not aware of any enemy presence, at least as far as you could notice, and that you would have known if otherwise.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: During the war, I had many such tasks, perhaps even up to a hundred. I did not attach importance to some of the things that happened, and I didn't even try to remember them, because these were regular tasks. As a matter of fact, I tried to forget certain things, so -- I mean, well, if that is written here, that might have happened, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, do you remember at what time you concluded this operation, the Ramljani -- in the Ramljani area on the 26th?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Oh, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember any -- having seen Mr. Sacic on that same day?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: On that day, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Markac on that day?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think it was on that day. After having completed this task, we were returning to Gracac, I think. Somewhere along the way, we were encountered by General Markac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This Chamber received evidence that at that occasion Mr. Sasic was present as well. Does this refresh your recollection?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No, I don't recall him being there. I don't think he was. I do know, however, that Mr. Janic accompanied Mr. Markac. I don't know whether there was anyone else there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, when, upon your return, you met -- or at least you saw Mr. Markac, could you describe what then happened?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: We were encountered by him along the road towards Gracac, I believe. We stopped, the vehicle column stopped. Some people got out, including myself. I saw that General Markac was there in conversation with a number of people who stood around him in a circle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember with whom he had a conversation, specifically?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. I did not approach them. I couldn't really see who he was addressing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us who the other group leaders were, and were they the same as the day before.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: You mean on the second day, the 26th?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Were the groups approximately the same, with the same group leaders, as on the 25th, or were the groups composed differently?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think the groups differed, that there were fewer. I think there were two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you remember who the group leaders were on the day before? That was the Plavno operation. Do you remember their names?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I was one group commander. The second person was Branko Balunovic. The third group commander was Bozo Krajina, and the fourth, Franjo Drljo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And who were group leaders on the 26th, the Ramljani operation?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I couldn't say. I think Bozo Krajina was with me. I think we were in one group, but I don't know for the other group. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was Mr. Drljo there on the 26th?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think he was. He was -- he should have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any specific recollection as to whether Mr. Drljo was engaged in that conversation with Mr. Markac?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think he was in the group of people addressed by Mr. Markac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us what matter was addressed by Mr. Markac at that moment?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I didn't come close, but I could see that Mr. Markac was angry over something. I think he mentioned some houses being burned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did he say anything about people being killed?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 7544 on the screen. Could we move to the second -- no. Before we do so, do you recognise this document? Have you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is a record of a witness interview held on the 16th of December last year with you. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, but I don't seem to recall it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you recall that you were interviewed as a witness on the 16th of December of last year?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Last year, in December, there was an interview, but I don't know whether it was on the 16th. In any case, there was an interview conducted with me on the premises of the County Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we move to the next page both in English and in B/C/S. I think for English, we have to go to the following page. One second, please. May we have page 3 in English. This is page 3. I'm sorry. Could we move it a little bit further down. In this record of your interview, you find a portion which relates to the events we just discussed; that is, at the lower part of the last big paragraph. You see that?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I read to you: "The next day, on the road between Knin and Gracac, we were intercepted by General Markac and Zdravko Janic, so we all exited the vehicles and surrounded them. General Markac was furious. He was shouting at Franjo Drljo specifically, saying that houses in the village were set on fire and that some people were killed, and then he told us to return directly to Zagreb ..." That is a different account compared to what you just told us. It is that you apparently were able to follow what Mr. Markac said, that he was specifically shouting at Franjo Drljo, and that he mentioned, apart from houses in the village being set on fire, that also some people were killed. Does this refresh your memory? It's a rather recent statement.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I did say that General Markac was surrounded by a group of people and that he was addressing someone. It seems I may have said that it was Franjo Drljo. I could see he was upset, and as I have already stated, I believe he mentioned certain houses which had been set on fire. I cannot recall exactly. But as for him mentioning any people being killed, well, I was trying to remember things, but I cannot say anything with any certainty. I wasn't close enough to be able to overhear every single word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And in last December, does this reflect what you stated when you were interviewed as a witness?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I do not understand. Does what reflect?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I just read to you, is that what you said in December when you were interviewed, so apart from whether this is what you recollect today?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: If this is the way it was written down, then I probably did say so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You do not contest or you do not claim that it was put on paper in an inaccurate way?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I believe it was taken down correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you see any houses burning on this 26th of August?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I saw that some houses had burned down recently. They were still smoldering. I couldn't tell, though, whether it took place a couple of hours before that or earlier. In any case, I think it had happened before our group entered the hamlet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have some difficulties in scrolling up to the previous portions of your testimony. Mr. Hedaraly, you have full access to the e-court, to --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'll give it another try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Equality of arms re-established. One second, please. Could you tell us, Mr. Zinic, how did your unit leave the area? When was it that it left the area?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think it was on the 26th. After we encountered General Markac, we went back to Gracac to collect our equipment, and then we went to Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That same evening, you left for Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you didn't stay overnight. Was there any meeting in the evening of the 26th you attended?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, did the whole of the Lucko unit leave that same evening for Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think it should have. I think we all returned, although I'm not sure. Some may have stayed behind, but I'm not certain of that. I think we all went back to Zagreb. If some people stayed, these were just individuals. I can't say anything other than that. I think we all went back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How did you travel back; all together in a bus, or separate in vehicles, or --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No, we went back to Zagreb in our vehicles. There were between four and six members of the unit per vehicle. We were in our official vehicles, off-road vehicles we had been assigned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you remember how many people participated in the 26th of August Ramljani area operation?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I think around 50 or 60.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any -- if I would suggest to you that Mr. Balunovic would have stayed in Gracac and not returned to Zagreb, does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Celic?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember having seen any of these two returning to Zagreb or do you have no recollection of it?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you at all whether I saw them or not. We all went in separate vehicles. I don't know who was in what vehicle. In my opinion, everyone should have returned to Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it planned that you would return to Zagreb on that same day?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because in your statement, I read that: "... and then he told us to return directly to Zagreb." Was there any reason to tell this if it was planned already?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I cannot comment on any plans. I wasn't aware of any. The only thing I can see now is what I seemingly stated when I said that General Markac told us we were all to go back to Zagreb. The task was completed, and we were sent back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you earlier told us that these search operations were in relation to the Freedom Train. Do you remember on what day the Freedom Train passed through the area?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If your operation was related to the voyage of the Freedom Train, were you aware of whether it had passed through the area, yes or no, because that apparently was one of the purposes of the operation?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Personally, I had no knowledge of the time it was supposed to go through or on what day. I cannot comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have no idea about the time it was supposed to get through. Do you know whether it had gone through already when you were still in the area?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the clock. Mr. Zinic, we'll first have a break, because it doesn't make sense to start a new subject at this very moment. We'd like to see you back in 25 minutes. We have a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zinic, we left off at the moment when the unit returned to Zagreb. Now, did you ever go back to Grubori or the Grubori area?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No, never again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to take you to a moment you mentioned earlier; that is, when you wrote a report on the events on the 25th of August. Do you remember where you wrote that report?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I remember that. We wrote that in Zagreb, in the headquarters of the unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, were you usually present in the premises where you wrote that report, if not in the field?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: There are no customary or established ways of drafting reports. One usually sits down in one's office or wherever is best at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you write your report in your own office?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I don't remember whether I was in my office or in another room. I don't know where I wrote it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us who asked you to write the report?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were ordered orally to do so by Josip Turkalj, the unit commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did he come to -- do you have an office in the headquarters? Do you have your own office there?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You had it on the 1st of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, I had it when I was employed there. I had a room where we -- how should I put it? Where we did the writing and where we kept our equipment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When you refer to the writing, you're not specifically referring to this report, but in general?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, it was an office, we can call it that, assigned to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, did Mr. Turkalj come to your office? What happened, exactly?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No, no. We were summoned to his office, all the commanders of the groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What did he -- you were together in his office when he addressed the matter?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were. We were all called to appear there, and he addressed us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What did he tell you, exactly?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: He said that a written order came in from the sector, from Sacic, stating that we, as group commanders, were to be tasked with drafting reports about the two days during which we were engaged in our activities in the area of Knin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does that mean that you had not yet written a report on the events of the 26th; that is, the Ramljani operation? Had you not yet written a report on that?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I had not, as far as I recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the report that was just shown to you before the break, was that produced also in Zagreb early September?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: In my previous statements, I couldn't even remember whether I had drafted any reports about the events on the second day. It was the last time I was interviewed that the report was shown to me. Before that, I wasn't even aware of having written it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have any recollection on having written such a report when you were in the field or on your return to Zagreb on the 26th, itself?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I truly cannot remember. I cannot answer this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it from your answer, that Mr. Turkalj told you that you had to write reports on the two days, that you had not yet written a report on the 26th?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think I hadn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, he told you that you had to write reports. He told you. Were all the group leaders present?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think all the group commanders were there, as well as Mr. Celic, who was acting commander. He was in Mr. Turkalj's office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, did you receive any information which would have to be included in your report or were you just given an order to write reports on the events of that day? What was it that you were instructed to do?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: We were told to draft a report each. I took it as such. Mr. Turkalj did not specify anything in particular as to what we were supposed to write about. Each of us was supposed to draft a report to the best of our recollections about the events in the field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you wrote that report. Did you write it by hand or --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: We usually drafted reports by hand, and then we would give that script to a secretary to type it in the computer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you have your own secretary or was it someone else's secretary?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: It was the unit commander's secretary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Again, do you remember where you wrote this report?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I usually wrote reports in my office. I think this was the case with this one as well. I don't think it was any other way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you deliver the handwritten report yourself to the secretary, or how did that go?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Usually, we gave it to her ourselves, and this was probably the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then once it was typed out, what would happen? Would you get it back or --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would get it back. I would get back the typed version, read it and then sign it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that what happened with your report that you drafted in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think so. It shouldn't have been anything different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was that the end of the story, as far as the report is concerned?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Once you had signed it, to whom would you give it? Or would you leave it with the secretary after having signed it?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think -- or, rather, it's not that I think. Probably it was given to the secretary, the secretary gave it to the commander, and the commander sent it by mail to the Sector of the Special Police, to Mr. Sacic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you receive any comment on the report you had given for being typed out? Did anyone comment on it?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. Did anyone comment on the report?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Celic say, Well, good report, or did he say -- was there anyone else, Mr. Sacic, Mr. Celic, Mr. Janic, whomever it may have been, that said, It's too long, or, It's too short, or is it just that you delivered it as it was, without any further comment?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, no. Once the report is written, it is sent to the sector, to Mr. Sacic. I mean, well, no further comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you ever see it back, that report, in those days? Well, let's say in 1995.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No. I saw that report again only sometime in 2000 something, when we were asked by the police to come in, when proceedings were initiated, in 2001 or 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So just for me to fully understand, you write a handwritten report, you deliver it to the secretary of Mr. Turkalj?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: She types it out, gives it to you for signature. Did you read it, whether she typed it out well?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I probably did. Usually, one does read it out. I did read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You signed it?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Signed it, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You delivered it for being sent up in the hierarchy?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You did not make -- did you make any corrections?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I mean, at one point I did see another report, too, where a correction had been made. I cannot say now whether -- well, I mean, I cannot say now whether I said that it should be corrected. I don't remember. I probably saw that something was omitted and I asked for a correction to be made, because corrections were made to reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was the correction?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, the first report, it did not include the fact that we were supposed to treat civilians in accordance with International Law in respect of civilian prisoners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When did you find out that the report was incomplete?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I don't even remember that. It's only when I was being questioned by the gentleman from the Tribunal. Casey, was that his name, Casey? Then he showed me the other one, and then I realised there were two. I think Casey, it was his name. When The Hague Tribunal was putting questions to me in Zagreb, I think it was 2004, that's when I saw this other report as well where the correction had been made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So when I earlier asked you whether once you had given the report for being typed out, you got it back for signature, and that you delivered it, that was the end of the story, apparently it was not, because a second version of the report was produced, or do you say -- I mean, could you tell us, you made the correction yourself?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, myself. But, you see, as far as reports were concerned, there was that possibility of having things added to them. That was the normal procedure for us; namely, that if a report was incomplete, an addition would be made. In this case, that is what was added, the correction, that is, because that had not been written out in the first place, that we should behave as we should.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did someone draw your attention to the fact that apparently something was missing?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I cannot answer that. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you consider it possible that someone else suggested that the report should be corrected or completed?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, there is that possibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I again put this question to you, and you know that you have to answer questions in accordance with the truth; that is, the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Did someone draw your attention to any correction or addition to be made to your report?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot give an answer because I do not remember that detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look at your report, and I'll take the second version. You apparently -- no, let's take the first, the first version. Can we have a look at P568. Do you recognise your signature?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I said that once already, that the signature could be mine, but I cannot state that with full certainty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we take you to the second report, which is P569. Could you have a look at that signature?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think it is. Well, you see, I changed the name [as interpreted] in which I signed my name, so I don't exactly remember. But I did sign my name this way before, so, yes, this is my signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, if you go to the content of the report, it says, second paragraph, that you held a brief meeting with Mr. Celic and then you split into three groups. Is my recollection correct that you said that there were four groups?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, we wrote the report from memory. Everybody wrote it up the way they remembered it. At that moment, if I wrote it was three groups, I may have made a mistake. I cannot say exactly. If it is written that there were three groups, there may have been three groups, but according to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take you to the large paragraph under the names, and I read to you that while you were on the left side of Grubori village, that there was certain fierce gun-fire and several explosions were heard. You asked about it over the system. You were told they had come up with a group of Chetniks. The fierce gun-fire and several explosions is not entirely the same as you told us today. Do you have an explanation for that? What you told us today, is that what happened, or was there fierce gun-fire and several explosions that you heard and that you were informed over the system on what had happened?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm making this statement on the basis of memory, so I cannot exactly remember all details. I mean, well, since the report says, and the report was written immediately after the events, perhaps that is the way things actually did happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it also says that some of the Chetniks were fleeing to the forest and that you immediately went after them, so that you did not even enter the village. Now, did you go after the Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, probably, yes, if that is what is written in this report, then that is probably the way things happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But earlier today, I think you gave testimony which is not in line with what is written here.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, in my testimony, I'm saying the things I can remember. I cannot speak about details if I don't remember them. It is only now, when I see these reports -- this report, the way it was written, then I think that is how things happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you aware of any of the reports drafted by the other group leaders were corrected as well?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that because I could not see their reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me put the following to you: This Chamber received evidence -- I'm not giving perhaps the entirety of the evidence, but I make a selection of it. The Chamber received evidence that the first reporting on the 25th was of a kind that nothing special had happened. Now, the Chamber also received evidence that this first report was then corrected or replaced, whatever you call it, where combat or at least exchange of fire appears, where it did not appear in a similar way in the first report. The Chamber also received evidence and has access to statements where you are supposed to have reported orally to Mr. Celic on the 25th that nothing special had happened on that day. Now, the Chamber looks at this report, which is dated the 25th of August, Gracac, although it was drafted in Zagreb at a later date, and the evidence could be interpreted as an effort to introduce combat in an organised way in the reports, where it had not been observed by those who were reporting. Did you understand what I suggested as a possible interpretation of that evidence?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I did not fully understand whether you are speaking of my two reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am speaking about your reports, your two reports, as an element in how one could interpret the evidence that I mentioned before; that is, that it was part of an effort to introduce combat where those writing the reports had not experienced such combat.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I mean, you are saying that someone else changed the report without my knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No one urged you to do that, not to change the -- well, the first report that one could -- and I'm seeking your answer to that, you could interpret the evidence as to be understood in the context of a joint effort to change the events in the report from "nothing special happened" to "exchange of fire, fierce gun-fire and explosions"?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, when presenting an oral report to Mr. Celic, in my group there was nothing that was happening. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But in this written report, you say you immediately went after them, the Chetniks, which is not in line with what you said you orally reported to Mr. Celic, did you?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, probably I didn't attach importance to that because I was just told that part of the Chetniks fled into the woods. Since I did not see anyone, there were no events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You didn't go after them, then, if you didn't see anyone, did you?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, what was said was that they had fled into the woods, and we went after them, but we didn't see anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I earlier -- but I have to check that. It is not my recollection that in your testimony earlier today, you referred to any such thing as the presence of Chetniks and going after them in the woods.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Again, I will note that my testimony is based on memory about things that happened 15 years ago. I really cannot remember details. Now, the report that is in front of me proves something different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That seems to be a conclusion. Are you aware of the position taken by Mr. Drljo in relation to writing reports about the 25th?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think that he did not write a report. I know that his position was that he did not wish to write, that he had nothing to write about. That's what we -- that's what he stated when we were at the commander's, when we were all together and when he had told us that we had to write reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did he get away with that, not to write a report, where he was ordered to write one?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I have no way of knowing. It is for the commander. He's the one who was supposed to resolve that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you told me that you do not remember whether anyone has drawn your attention to this added element in the report. I also asked you about whether specific information should be contained in the report you are ordered to write in Zagreb. Can you, with certainty, tell us that you were not told by anyone what elements -- what factual elements should be contained in your report, or is it also a matter you don't remember?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: When talking to the commander, when it was said that we should write reports, we probably discussed it, or perhaps I discussed it with someone, since we were supposed to write reports had something happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "With someone." Can you be more precise? Did you discuss the content -- did you discuss the events at the moment you were ordered to write a report? Was there any conversation about what had actually happened?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I probably asked sort of whether anything had happened. Now, I could have talked to Mr. Balunovic, or Bozo Krajina, or Drljo, or Celic, since we worked together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the events on which you are supposed to report were discussed. Is there anything in your report which may have been the fruit of that discussion rather than of your own observation; that is, that you heard that it had happened or someone said that this is what happened, without you having personal knowledge of it, but including it in your report?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, when I was out in the field in all of these actions, there was shooting, and that was probably the case in this task in Grubori. It is hard to distinguish between and among different actions. They were all similar, more or less. And we tried -- or at least I tried to forget all about them as soon as I could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is not an answer to my question. My question is whether, in your report, possibly events -- facts are described which you discussed, when invited to write a report, with others, rather than on the basis of a clear recollection of the events, a clear recollection of what you observed during that 25th of August.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I was supposed to write a report about a group that was under my command. I may have talked to some of the members of my group. I really cannot remember. Perhaps it was one of them. Perhaps I asked them whether they knew something, whether they could explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you introduced a second element. The first is that you may have had a conversation with the group leaders. Did you also have a conversation with all of your group members?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Oh, no, most certainly not. It must have been someone I was closer to, someone I thought could help me. But, I mean, I really cannot remember. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Still I have got no answer to my question. My question was whether you consider it a possibility that what others had observed and what the recollection of others was may have been presented in the report for a fact, although you did not personally observe it and it's not based on your personal recollection of the events.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Reports were written based on my opinion, as a commander, and by the opinions of those who participated in the operation. If I am supposed to draft a report and I lack information, then, of course, I turn to those who took part in it to get by certain information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it may be that information you obtained from others, including those who were not members of your unit, that may have ended up in the report as a fact?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This Chamber has seen a statement in which one of the other group leaders stated that all the group leaders had received a piece of paper on which they based their reports. Did you receive any paper on which you based your report?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know that you didn't or do you think that you didn't?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. On that day in Zagreb, were you aware of casualties in Grubori?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: You mean the day the report was written?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of it that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When did you become aware?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult to say. At a certain point after a while, I don't even know when, it is then that I heard that there had been certain things there, but it was in passing during an informal conversation. There was nothing specific about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you never heard about any television coverage, relatively soon after the event, in which casualties in Grubori were discussed or were the subject of the reporting?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: There was some, but I didn't connect that to our unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And no one did in your unit?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I didn't discuss it with others. I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One final question. Mr. Celic was there when Mr. Turkalj called you in his office in order to receive an order to write a report?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you, to some extent, discussed the events amongst yourselves, those who were present in that office?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: We probably did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But in that discussion, do you know for certain that no dead bodies found in Grubori were ever mentioned during that conversation?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I don't think it was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why do you think it was not mentioned?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I can't say with any certainty whether it was mentioned or wasn't. But as for what you mentioned about TV broadcasts about the casualties, that is something I did not discuss with my unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you did discuss, then, without referring to the television broadcast, events such as casualties that may have occurred in that area?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I cannot decide on the sequence of things, whether there may have been broadcasts before or after that. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm focusing on what was the subject of conversation in that office in Zagreb where you were called in order to receive an instruction to write a report.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: You mean on what date?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am inquiring whether dead bodies found in Grubori were part of the conversation which took place in that office when you were ordered to write a report.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I allow for the possibility of having discussed such matters there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if you earlier -- when I said whether you were aware of casualties when you were in that office, when you said, No, I was not aware, that you correct that now and say, I may have been aware because it may have been the subject of our conversation?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I can't say how long it took. After I received the order to draft my report, I left. I think some stayed behind, but I don't know whether they discussed such matters. I know for a fact that we didn't all leave at that point. Some remained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zinic, you said that there was a conversation. You didn't say, I left the office and others might have a conversation. You clearly pointed at a conversation and even did not exclude for the possibility that what you heard there may have found its way into your report. Now you are, more or less, telling us, There may have been a conversation, but I wasn't there, which is inconsistent with your previous testimony today.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I wasn't trying to say that I left immediately, while the commander was issuing orders to draft our reports. Following that, there was probably a very brief conversation about the events there. Given that there were no events to report on along my axis, I left to write the report. As for those who stayed, I don't know what they discussed. Again, I must say that I'm now talking about something which took place --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am aware of that. But you earlier, in your testimony, did not exclude that in that conversation, the presence of dead bodies had been included in the subject of conversation? You said it may have been part of the conversation?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I'm speaking from memory. I can't say anything with 100 per cent certainty, especially whether this was discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has no further questions for you, Mr. Zinic. I am -- I would like to inquire with the parties whether they could give an estimate on the time they would need for cross-examination. Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It's a little difficult, seeing the answers that we may get, but I think one session, at the most, should be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Other parties. Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: One or two sessions, Your Honour, depending on what is covered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I only have one question, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you prefer to have the break first and then have a long session - that would mean approximately one hour and 25 minutes, Mr. Hedaraly - where you would try to finish even within that time, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I think if I start now, it may be better to have the break in the middle so I can assess what can be cut at that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zinic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Hedaraly, and Mr. Hedaraly is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Hedaraly, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Zinic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can have 65 ter 7655 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we -- Mr. Hedaraly, before we continue, I referred to statements. I read the relevant portions into the transcript. It was not on my mind to have them in evidence, since I was focusing exclusively on those specific portions, and I'm especially referring to the December 2009 statement. If the parties would take a different view, I'd like to know that. But as matters stand now, reading the relevant portions is sufficient, as far as the Chamber is concerned. I hear of no objections to this approach. Mr. Hedaraly, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If I could have 65 ter 7655 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
