utterances.text: Mr. Zinic, you were promoted to assistant commander of the special police in November of 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, can I have 65 ter 7655 admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently no objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit P2717. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P2717 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Zinic, I want to go back to the operation on the 25th of August, around the village of Grubori. Now, before -- at the beginning of the operation, in the morning, you had a briefing with Mr. Celic; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't exactly call it a briefing. Once we reached our starting point, we simply received our tasks and were issued with maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: But you received some instructions from Mr. Celic at that point?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And Mr. Celic warned you that there may be civilians in these villages who were registered by UNPROFOR, and that you if saw them, you should leave them alone; is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: It probably is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you also stated you were -- there were four groups on that day; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I stated that from memory. I'm slightly confused now, though, because it seems that in my report there is a mention of three. I do think that there were four in the field. I don't know why this is --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And, in fact, you'd named them for the Trial Chamber. It was Mr. Balunovic, Mr. Krajina, Mr. Drljo, and yourself, according to your memory; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And according to your memory, you were at the left -- you were the group the most at the left during this operation; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me show you a map. It's 65 ter 7592. Can you take a few moments and look at this map, and tell me if this is -- this accurately represents your recollection of the operation on the 25th of August, in terms of the axes of movement of the Lucko unit?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: It should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. President, can I have 65 ter 7592 in evidence, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit P2718. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the absence of any objections, P2718 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And before I move on, I just want to clarify something. I may have been confused at the beginning of your examination. When you reached the top -- the Orlovac peak, that's the first time that all the groups merged together on the 25th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And the village of Grubori was before you reached that peak; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And when you were discussing with the Chamber the hamlet or village that you had -- where you met at the end, that was at the end of the operation, when you met with Mr. Celic at the end point; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, I want to go back, during the operation, when you heard some shooting. Now, the shooting that you heard was coming from your right; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you then tried to contact someone on your Motorola to find out what was happening?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Usually, if there is anything going on, you try to find out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And the general rules are that if you hear shooting, you stop, you find cover, and you see how events unfold; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, in such events, for personal safety, one stops at the very position you find yourself to be at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And then did you receive a response to your message on the radio saying that it will be checked, what the shooting was or what you were reporting?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I cannot say at all whether we had radio communication at that point in time. I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Well, you just told me that you remember contacting someone to find out what was happening.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I cannot claim it was so. I was trying to do that, but I don't know whether I succeeded.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me show you the statement that you gave - that was taped - to the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter 7546, and if I could then go to page 133, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And if you want to have a few minutes to look at the pages before or after, just ask me, but my question is very specific to one portion and to see if that refreshes your memory. If you see at line 5 in English, it's line 8 in the B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could we have a date --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: -- a date, please, for the interview?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I want to say it's November 2004, but if you just bear with me. 15th of November, 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And here, you see the question is: "RC," for Mr. Casey, "Okay. You said just now that you -- you went on your radio and to try and find out what the situation is; is that correct?" You answered: "Yes." Then the next question is: "And what was the response you got the first time you called up?" And then you answer: "I can't even say who answered my call, but the answer -- I can't say who was the person who answered it, but they said that the shooting is going on and that they will check. "Q. And they will check -- "A. It will be checked."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, several words in that answer are not translated accurately, so there's definitely a translation issue with the answer from Croatian into English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I invite you at least, during the next break, to share your information with Mr. Hedaraly, because to clarify this matter in the presence of the witness, that would take quite some time. And I think if you would agree on it, and perhaps you have a language assistant that could help you, Mr. Hedaraly, then we might be able to do that immediately -- to hear from you immediately after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: We could do that, and I could give you the reference. I can just give you the line number, Your Honour, without saying what the words are. It's line 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zinic, do you speak or understand English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very little.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take off your earphones for a second. Mr. Kuzmanovic, there's a word missing?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah, two words, actually. The words -- on line 18, the third and fourth word from the end are not translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you inform the Chamber as to what you understand the portion which is not translated? And I know that you're not a sworn translator, but that we have an idea on how important the matter is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I can just read the words in Croatian, Your Honour, if that's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: "Vjerojatno, mozda."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I have not yet received the translation of these -- not a translation, but the interpretation of what you just said. Could you repeat them?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly. [Interpretation] "Likely, perhaps."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Without the context, it means nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then at least we know what is bothering you, Mr. Kuzmanovic, without drawing any conclusions at this moment. Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can the witness be instructed to put back his earphones? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Zinic, the portion I read to you, does that refresh your memory as to any answers you may have received on the radio on 25th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we ask the witness to read his answer? Mr. Hedaraly, we will invite the witness, and we will see whether it can be enlarged, line 18 and 19. Could you please read that in your own language, Mr. Zinic, and then answer the question that Mr. Hedaraly put to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know. I can't even say who picked up my call. Probably maybe someone who had heard me. The answer was that there was shooting, that they will check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's not the question that was put to you. Well, reading, you read it out aloud, and I think we received some information, although we were not seeking that at this very moment. Mr. Hedaraly, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, reading this, these lines, does that refresh your memory as to whether, in fact, someone did answer your call on 25 of August, when you asked what was going on after having heard shooting?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I wanted to say that I can't recall it. I wanted to say that someone may have heard it, may have answered, but I can't say with any certainty who it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. Let me move on. Now, after having heard that shooting and trying to contact someone, you moved towards the village where the shots were coming from; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I think, since the communications were not working, I tried to contact someone who was on my right-hand side, on the right-hand flank. I must say that in such situations, that's the rule, that is what you try to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: My question was not whether you tried to communicate with someone else. My question is: You moved towards that direction. Was that to try to have a physical contact with the unit -- the group on your right, so you moved towards the direction where the shooting was coming from?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, in my view, if things could not be checked by way of communications, the rule was to try to link up with the group that was closer to what was going on, and that may have been the case then too.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you or did you not move towards the village -- towards the direction where you heard shooting?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think I did move in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you. And that took you at the edge or at the outskirts of, as you called it, the hamlet of Grubori; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I cannot claim whether it was a hamlet or whether it was Grubori. I think that I met up with someone who was on my right. Now, who that was and whether I actually did link up, I cannot say that now with any degree of certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: But you did reach what appeared to be the beginning of a hamlet or a village. You saw some houses there, and my understanding from your testimony is you did not go in the village or the hamlet, but you were right at the outskirts of it. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I did not see the village and I did not enter it. But when I turned to the right, I reached a clearing, a meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And when you reached that point, you saw some houses on fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I did not see houses visually from that spot. I just saw something that looked like smoke, as if something was on fire or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me get back to this. Let me go to page 139 of this interview that is on the screen now. And there is, at line 13 in the English, line 16 in the B/C/S, the question is put to you: "Okay. So did you and the men under your command take up a position anywhere near the village of Grubori?" And your answer: "So we reached one of the groups at the edge of the village. We did not enter the village. After we reached one of our groups, we turned back to the line of the search and continued with it." Does that refresh your memory as to whether you came to the edge of the village of Grubori on the 25th of August?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: It's hard to say now. You say that I got to the village of Grubori. I cannot claim that, because I did not see the buildings. Had I linked up with one of the groups, well, that is probably true, that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That you did what? I didn't understand the last part of your answer. What is it true that you probably did?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I'm saying this now on the basis of memory. I assume this is how things developed. I know that I turned right, that I reached a meadow, a group there, and that we linked up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And when you arrived there, you also saw other members of the Lucko unit leaving Grubori; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I saw a group coming from the direction of -- well, the direction of that smoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. And in that group were a number of people, including Mr. Drljo, Mr. Beneta, and Mr. Delimar; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Well, is it yes or is it not yes?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think it's yes. Well, yes. I mean, you are leading me now to say something on the basis of memory, whether it was that way or not. Since there were several people there, I cannot say with full certainty that they were coming exactly from that direction, specifically from the direction of the village of Grubori.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Well, let me show you what you told the investigative judge in Croatia in December of last year, a few months ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can have 65 ter 7544 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And the Presiding Judge showed you this document a little earlier. And before I ask you specific questions from it, as soon as it comes up on the screen, if we can go to the last page. Is that your signature at the bottom right? Well, top right in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And it also says that that record was read back to you and that you listened to the judge's dictation, and you therefore signed it. Do you remember doing that?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you also remember being cautioned before the interview that giving a false statement was a criminal offence?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me go to page 3 in the English and page 2 of the B/C/S. And in the English, in the paragraph that starts at the middle of the page, the third sentence on the fourth line in the English, after the list of names, the first four names that are mentioned, the sentence after the next one says: "To the next question by the same person, I answer that I saw about 15 members of the Lucko Anti-Terrorist Unit leaving the village of Grubori, and among them I recognised Berislav Galic, Franjo Drljo, Igor Beneta, Ivica Delimar, and Marijan Husko, but I do not remember the others." Now, did you remember saying that to the judge in December of last year?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So you told him that they were leaving the village of Grubori. Does that refresh your memory today as to whether these members were leaving the village of Grubori?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say with full certainty. When I gave this a bit of thought later on, maybe it wasn't the village of Grubori. I cannot say with 100 per cent certainty that it was from Grubori that they were coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And if we go up to the previous paragraph on the same page, about five or six lines from the bottom of that paragraph, you also say: "I saw some houses on fire in the village of Grubori." Does that refresh your memory as to whether you had seen any houses on fire in Grubori?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Again, I will repeat what I said. Now, whether that was the village or hamlet of Grubori, I cannot claim that with 100 per cent certainty. I spoke on the basis of memory, the direction that they were coming from. I mean, I assume that they were coming from the village of Grubori.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: When you saw your colleagues from the Lucko unit leaving or coming from the direction of Grubori, what did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, they didn't tell me anything. I probably asked someone what had happened, and he probably answered that nothing had happened, that the Chetniks were fleeing into the hills and that we were chasing after them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Well, "nothing happened" and "Chetniks are fleeing up the hill and we're chasing them" is not the same thing, is it?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, in these events we do not attach importance to this regular kind of thing that happens. We always go ahead. What had already happened no longer matters. Maybe someone told me that nothing had happened or that there was nothing that was important that they were supposed to tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: The whole purpose of these mopping-up operations were to make sure that there were no Chetniks or enemy soldiers or terrorists in those hamlets, so are you telling me that information about possible Chetniks that are fleeing is not significant?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No, no, you misunderstood me. I am not saying that that was irrelevant, that the Chetniks were fleeing and that we were after them. That was our priority. They were fleeing, and we were chasing after them. So what had happened before was no longer important.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So why did you tell the investigative judge, and it's at the bottom paragraph on that page, that they told you nothing happened, when, in fact, they told you that there were Chetniks there and that you had to chase them?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say. I probably asked what happened, and they said, Nothing, the Chetniks are fleeing. You see, perhaps you find that strange. Communication among us in the field is that way, it's simple.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me just, for the record, go to your interview with the Office of the Prosecutor in 2004, 7546 -- 65 ter 7546.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And since these are not in evidence, I'll just briefly, Mr. President, move through a few items just for the record. And if I can go to page 139 first. And, Your Honour, we can take the break right after this exercise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: You see, first of all, just for context, at the bottom of page 139, when you said that you reached the edge of the village, then there was a question: "Did you remain with one of your groups for a period of time?" If we can turn the page. And your answer then was: "When we reached this -- this group of our men, we were -- it was told that somebody had run away to the hills, so basically we returned to our line of search and continued in that direction." Then if we move forward to page 144, at line 16 the question is put to you: "Okay, you say that you heard a message saying that some people had fled. Do you know who relayed that message?" Then again you say that it was said that somebody had escaped through the bushes, towards the mountaintop, that you tried to move back the search lines. And, finally, page 151, at the bottom, for the third time you mention that men had ran away from that village. And then I just showed you, to the judge you said that the response you got from your colleagues was that nothing had happened, and I understood your answer to mean that both of these things could have been said. And just before we take the break, I just want to confirm that you, yourself, you did not see any terrorist, or any Chetnik, or anyone else, for a matter of fact, except colleagues of yours from the Lucko unit on that day. Correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zinic. Mr. President, if we could have the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have the break, and we'll resume at 10 minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Zinic, on the 25th of August, you also did not see anyone from your unit with a prisoner that day; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Either during the operation, at the end of it, or at any time did you see a prisoner with anyone from your unit on the 25th of August?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you also testified, if I understood correctly, that after the operation, you never really knew what happened in Grubori later that day or the following days. Right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, you stated to the investigative judge in Croatia that a year ago or so, you heard that Igor Beneta and Ivica Delimar may have been responsible for the liquidations and arsons in Grubori. Do you remember saying that to the investigative judge?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, the question was whether I had perhaps heard that in informal conversations. It was said somewhere, but it could be all sorts of things. It can also be misconstrued, planted. I mean, I didn't take it seriously.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: But that's just something that you heard informally recently; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't recently, it was a few years ago, but it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And can you -- do you know which group Mr. Beneta and Mr. Delimar were part of on the 25th of August?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Were they in your group?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think they weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And after arriving to the edge of Grubori or to the location where you saw your colleagues come from, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I probably asked what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: We talked about you asking what was going on and what the response was. After that, did you just carry on with your search or resume to your position and carried out with your search?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, no. I think it was said that Chetniks were fleeing into the woods, that there had been some kind of conflict, that the Chetniks were fleeing into the woods, and that they should be chased.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you actually chase them?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me go to page 157 of the interview with the Office of the Prosecutor that is on the screen. And at the bottom, the question starts -- I'm interested in your answer on the next page, but for the full reference, at line 25: "So at some point, did you come ... that it would be better to resume the search in the direction that you originally started?" Then there was a confusion, and then the question was rephrased: "Okay. So at some point, did you feel that you'd lost the people that you were chasing out there?" And then if you turn the page, your answer is: "I mean, we generally did our job. We did -- we were following our line of search. We only paid attention in case we -- you know, to spot somebody, we just followed the procedure the way you're supposed to." Then you say: "It would be wrong to say that we chased after them. That would be wrong, because we did not chase after them." So, Mr. Zinic, did you or did you not chase these Chetniks on 25th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I didn't see them. I was told that they were fleeing into the woods. And what it says here, "jurnuli," "rushed after them," we didn't do things that way. That is not the way we operate, and that would not be logical. Since I had my direction in which I was supposed to move, it was only natural that I would go back to my direction of movement. Now, what you said, whether we found them, we were going after them. I did not see them. I didn't see them afterwards, either, or before that moment, when I was told that the Chetniks were fleeing into the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: But you did not make any changes to go after them? You simply went back to your original route and carried on with your operation as you had before the shooting -- you heard the shooting; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, due to the configuration of the terrain, you seem to feel that you're moving along a flat land. However, it was a very unfavorable configuration; bushes, rocks, crevasses. It wasn't easy to move in a particular direction. You had to overcome certain natural obstacles. It wasn't easy to move fast. It was raining, it was foggy, visibility was very limited. From time to time, there was fog or the clouds would be low, and at some points in time, you couldn't see further than, say, 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can you please repeat for me the word that you said was the chasing after, the rushing after? Can you repeat it in B/C/S, please, when you read the portion of your statement?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: You'll have to repeat that for me. In which line was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I think it's at line 11 of the page that's on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: "Jurnuli," that means to go after them quickly, to rush after them. That's why I said that that was wrong. We moved as the configuration of the terrain allowed us to move.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So what you're saying is that when you chased these Chetniks, you didn't rush after them; you simply carried on along the usual speed and were looking for them. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, something like that. That would be classical search of the terrain, of course, with a higher degree of caution due to the possibility of having contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I want to briefly touch upon your report or your reports for that day. I know it has been discussed extensively, so I don't want to go through the whole story. But when you were told to write this report by Mr. Turkalj, what information, other than your memory, did you use to prepare your report?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: As I said, I probably contacted someone from my group and I asked him. Probably we came to some kind of a conclusion. I asked whether he knew anything, and probably -- I mean, well, I cannot say exactly now, but I probably was talking to someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you know who that person you probably were talking to in your group was? We can look at the list of names in your report, if you want, if that can help you.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No, I think -- no, I cannot remember now. I really cannot help you at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So you probably talked to someone in your group, and I think you said you also probably discussed these events with the other group leaders that were in Mr. Turkalj's office. Correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, we talked in relation to what had happened and because of the order that had been received, and a report had to be written, which I found logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you also rely on other reports? Did someone give you another report, prepared by someone else, to use as a guide?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And did you include anything in your report that was based on conversations either with the person in your group you talked to or the other group leaders, but that you did not, yourself, witness that day?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, probably someone did tell me, in conversation, that there had been a clash with the Chetniks in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So your report -- your report is not based only on your recollection of the events that happened, but also on this other information that you may have learned from these other people; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, it's logical that I would ask the members of my group, because I was writing a report about the work of the entire group, whether there had been something that should be written up in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm not asking you whether it's logical or not that you would ask them. I asked you that: Your report was also based on these conversations with other people that you had and not only on your own recollection; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, we can say yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, have you talked to anyone involved in the Grubori operation about the events in Grubori since then? I mean, in recent years. Let me rephrase that question. I'm sorry. Other than the statements and interviews you gave to various authorities, did you talk to anyone from the Lucko unit about what happened in Grubori in the recent years?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: When did you talk to -- who did you talk to?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I talked to Marko Krpan.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you talk to anyone else?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And Mr. Krpan was in your group on the 25th of August; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were together.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Is it possible that he is the person you contacted, after Mr. Turkalj ordered you to write the report, to discuss with him?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you talk to Mr. Drljo about the incidents -- about the incident in Grubori?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No, not with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you talk to Mr. Drljo about anything in the last, let's say, 10 years?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, we are on -- we are not on speaking terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Why are you not on speaking terms?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, that's how he is. He refuses to talk to me or to someone. It's his right, it's his attitude.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know someone called Bozidar Smotalic? And for the record, that's S-m-o-t-a-l-i-c.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And do you know anyone called Zvonko Pausic, P-a-u-s-i-c?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Zvonko Pausic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And he was the commander of the Zlatar Special Police Unit in 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me show you two statements that Mr. Pausic and Mr. Smotalic gave, where they discuss apparently a conversation that they witnessed between you and Mr. Drljo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And if we can have 65 ter 7657, and the second one is 65 ter 7658. And just for the record, they are exactly identical, except for the name of the person who gave the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And I just want you to look at it and just comment briefly if that is accurate -- if that is consistent with your recollection. Maybe if you just read it, it's going to be easy -- simpler than me reading it on the record. And maybe we can turn the page in the English just for everyone to see the end. Please let me know when you are finished reading. Have you had a chance to read that document?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And is that a conversation that you had with Mr. Drljo that is recorded there?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: There was an attempt at conversation, but I think it was before this time. Drljo tried to speak with me about the reports. However, as I can see, we ended that conversation by him saying that I wrote that report in 1997 on Sacic's order. I tried to tell him that it was in 1995 and that it is incorrect that it took place in 1997. The only thing I don't know is the thing about Bozidar Smotalic. I don't know who he is. I don't think he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: What is reported in this report, that is essentially an accurate reflection of a conversation that you had with Mr. Drljo; is that what I have to understand?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is completely wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: What is completely wrong?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: The fact that Smotalic was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Leaving aside the presence of Mr. Smotalic, what is recorded there as a conversation between you and Mr. Drljo, just the contents of that conversation, leaving aside who was present, is that a conversation that you had with Mr. Drljo that is reported there or is it not?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No, this was not the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: What was the conversation that you remember having with Mr. Drljo about the reports? Without referring to that document, from your memory, what is the conversation you remember having with Mr. Drljo?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, he came to me to speak about the reports which were written. He was trying to say that we drafted those reports on Sacic's orders and that we had to put in what he told us, as well as that we wrote that in 1997. I told him that that was not true. We didn't write it in 1997, and we did not write it on Sacic's orders. The reports were written based on Turkalj's oral order conveying Mr. Sacic's written orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Was Mr. Zvonko Pausic present at that conversation you had with Mr. Drljo?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, because I did not read it in the record, it may make sense just to have these two documents in evidence. I can state for the record that these were statements that were found during the search of Mr. Drljo's residence. That is the information we have. I don't know if they should be admitted under seal, if they are admitted for that reason. I just don't think it's worth reading it on the record. The witness testified about it, and maybe for the sake of completeness, we can have those marked and admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, generally I don't have an objection, but we just really don't have a foundation as to a date or really any foundation from where -- other than what Mr. Hedaraly talked about, the documents having been found in a search at -- of Mr. Drljo's apartment. I don't necessarily have an objection to the admission of these documents, but I'd just like a little bit more of a foundation laid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, let me -- there is a conversation that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I take it that it's not really an objection, so therefore that's no reason not to admit it, and therefore I consider this to be a request from Mr. Kuzmanovic to provide him with all information you have available, and if that's not complete, then to see whether we can find more information .

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any other observation? If not, Mr. Registrar, the two documents would be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 65 ter document 7657 shall be assigned Exhibit P2719. And 65 ter document 7658 shall be assigned Exhibit P2720. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Just for my information, you say they are the same as the -- apart from the name. Is the signature different? Is it the signature of the person who took the statement or who gave the statement? And if you'd just show it on the screen and then we have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I only have the English version with me so if we can have both of them side by side in the original, I think we'll be able to ascertain that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of the other one?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes, the two originals, if we can have them side by side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One is with a kind of a -- yes, I see that one is with and the other one is without a signature, and there's some handwritten text which says "illegible." Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just check. P2719 and P2720 are admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Zinic, let's move to the second date, the Ramljani operation on the 26th of August. And can you just confirm that there was an operation the following day in Ramljani?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you testified earlier today, and if you don't remember, I can pull up your exact words, but you essentially testified that on your line of the operation, nothing had happened and that you had not come under fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And I think the Presiding Judge showed you your report for the day of Ramljani, where you said that you did come under fire. Can you explain for the Court the discrepancy between your testimony that you did not come under fire and your report stating that you did come under fire?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: It is probably due to my memory. In my view, I don't think there were any events on the second day. I had gone through a number of operations, and things get mixed up. It's very difficult for me to say whether something happened a day or two later or before that, or a month, for that matter --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And at the end of the operation, you were intercepted by Mr. Markac and Mr. Janic; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And I know we went into some detail earlier -- or you went into some detail with the Chamber about that incident. And if we can just have, once again, 65 ter 7544, which is your statement to the investigative judge. And the Presiding Judge read you a portion of it. I want to just read you the portion that is following. It's page 3 in the English and page 2 in the B/C/S. At the very bottom of the page in the English, that's the portion the Presiding Judge read to you, that General Markac was furious, he was shouting at Franjo Drljo specifically, saying that houses in the village were set on fire and that some people were killed. And then: "He told us to return directly to Zagreb ..." If we can turn the page in the English: "... and said that people will be fired." Now, to your knowledge, Mr. Zinic, was anyone from the Lucko unit ever fired either for the incidents in Grubori or those in Ramljani?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you were sent back to Zagreb that day. Were you aware that there were other units of the special police that stayed behind and carried on operations on the 27th and 28th of August?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I am not sure. Perhaps a part of the unit did stay in the field, indeed. I don't know, in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether you were aware that other units of the special police, other than the Lucko unit, did stay behind and did carry out operations in the field on the 27th and 28th of August. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I did not, but I did hear that some units did remain after that date, although I'm not familiar with any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you said that after that -- after you got intercepted by Mr. Markac, and you went back to Gracac to collect your equipment and then left for Zagreb, how long did you spend in Gracac at that time?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: You mean on that day when we went back to Gracac to pick up our equipment and how much time we spent there? Probably the time we needed to pack up and go towards Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can we have P606 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I just have a few more questions for you, Mr. Zinic. And you'll see a report from the Lucko unit from 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can go to page 83 in B/C/S and page 5 in the English. And, Your Honour, just for the Court's information, only a portion of the document was translated, the one that dealt with 1995. That's why the B/C/S version is much larger, but it's highly irrelevant. It talks about 1991 and so on. And this is the report of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We hear of no objections against this partial translation, so therefore please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So this is the section on Operation Storm. And if we go to page 85 in the B/C/S and the next page, page 6, in the English, there's a sentence at the very top in the B/C/S, and in the English it's the third paragraph, the last sentence, where it says: "Mr. Drazan Curkovic, deputy commander of the Lucko ATJ, and Assistant Commanders Josip Celic and Stjepan Zinic commanded the unit in the field." Is that accurate statement as to your role during Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: No, I was not assistant commander in Operation Storm. I was a specialist training instructor at the time. I saw that the report was drafted in 1998. Is that correct? The author was probably not familiar with the fact that I was not assistant commander. I wasn't appointed assistant commander by that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And other than the title of assistant commander, is it correct that you commanded these units in the field with Mr. Celic and Mr. Curkovic?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, I did. I did have command responsibility in certain operations which took place, since I had the rank of instructor, and I did carry out command duties. I also wanted to say that it only happened in such cases when all those senior to me were absent. Only in such circumstances did I assume command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. I just want briefly to move backwards in time now to the 7th of August. And if we move to one page before in the B/C/S, and it's the same page in the English, it says that your unit, together with the joint forces, at 1400 hours prevailed. I assume it's in the broader area of Donji Lapac. Now, is it correct that the special police were the first units of the Croatian armed forces that entered Donji Lapac?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I think it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And that was on the 7th of August, correct, 1995?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I cannot confirm the dates. It doesn't ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Well, looking at the report, in the English, it's the page before, but you have it in your language in front of you. Do you have any reason to believe that that date is inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Concerning your question about Donji Lapac?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes, that it was on the 7th of August?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Well, no, I can't say whether it is correct or not. I cannot recall the date; hence, I cannot comment at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. And how long did you stay in Donji Lapac before moving on to the border area, as I understand?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: In my opinion, I think we stayed until nightfall. I believe by that time of day, we had movement to other areas, although I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And when you entered Donji Lapac, there were only a few houses on fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether I saw a few. There may have been a house here or there, but I wouldn't say a few or several.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And after Donji Lapac, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I'm really not sure. I don't know. I don't know where we went.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me just --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: Somewhere towards the border with Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me just briefly, in the little time remaining, go to your interview again, 65 ter 7544, hoping it can refresh your memory. It's at page 84.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Counsel. 7544 is a three-page document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: 65 ter 7544. I apologise. Oh, 65 ter 7546. I'm sorry. That's the interview. The number was the statement. Thank you, Mr. Kuzmanovic. Go to page 84, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And there's a brief summary here of your activity on the first day, starting at line 17, and you can read it as I read the English: "So by my calculations, then - correct me if I'm wrong - on the first day you advanced down the Velebit, the second day you advanced to the Gospic-Gracac road, the third day you believe was a free day, the fourth day you advanced on Lapac and then went to the Bosnian border, and on the fifth day you returned to Zagreb, you believe?" And at that time in 2004, you said: "Yes, according to how I think, yes." Does that refresh your memory as to your movements on those days?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I cannot be certain as to where we were in the course of those few days, but this is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And do you remember when you left on the 8th of August? Was it at night or was it the following day?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN ZINIC
utterances.text: I don't even know where we started from. I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you ever go back to Donji Lapac after first going there and leaving?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I know that we've covered this with many other witnesses, I know that the Chamber didn't ask any questions regarding this issue, so I think -- I mean, we've gone into it some, but we're beyond the scope of what the Chamber's discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just trying to recover my -- what I read in the beginning of this session as to the subject matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It's on page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber also informed the parties that questions may touch on events. They did not, however. That was in order to give you an opportunity to prepare for that in case we would. I think it was clear that the other parts, that we would certainly deal with those, and that the Chamber was still considering whether or not to deal, in its examination, with this first portion. We decided not to do that. So I think it's fair to say that your cross-examination -- of course, cross-examination is always, in view of Chamber witnesses, a bit odd, but would go beyond what we find in Rule 90(H), I think it is. Unless, of course, you could say that this is a matter which could -- would be -- would support your case. At the same time, that's, of course, expected to be done when the parties are presenting their evidence, where we have -- at least for the time being, we have left that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, as you may have noticed, it was not an area that was particularly -- of particular interest. That's why I kept it for the end. So if the Chamber prefers, I have no problems in completing my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from that, the clock might encourage you to do that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, if you would have a fair expectation that you could elicit something entirely new in this respect, the Chamber considers it appropriate that you not go over the same ground again which was dealt with in quite some detail with quite many witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. But when we had a witness here that may have been present, it seemed incumbent upon us to at least address it with the witness. But I understand the Chamber's guidance, and as I said, that's the only reason why we proceeded, not to then be told that we can't -- that we haven't fulfilled that Rule 90(H) obligation in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, will certainly not --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sure, I understand that, Your Honour. I mean, the OTP took two statements of this person prior to trial, and if they wanted to elicit that testimony, they could have called it in their case in chief. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think that Mr. Hedaraly announced that he had finished his cross-examination. Mr. Kuzmanovic, as matters stand now, could you -- are you still on the same estimate?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Roughly, Your Honour. I think I could -- one to one and a half. I don't think I need two full sessions, Your Honour. It may be less, depending on what my review reveals this evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll do my best to keep it to one, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, I'm not -- I'm thinking at this moment, Mr. Kuzmanovic. Could we move into private session for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We will adjourn, and the trial will resume on Thursday, the 15th of April, quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon, Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th day of April, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.06 p.m.,
